full_judgment:
Md Mozammel Hoque J : This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why they should not be directed to grant Division-I (Class-I) ,to the petitioner in Dhaka Central Jail is connection with Lalbagh PS Case No. 11(11)75 as under-trial prisoner. 

 2. It is stated in the application that the petitioner was an Army Officer in Bangladesh Army with a good record of service and reputation. He comes of an enlightened distinguished well-to-do Muslim family of this country. The petitioner was arrested by the Police on 13-8-1996 in connection with the aforesaid case. At the time of his arrest he was serving in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as Director-General in the rank and status of Joint Secretary of the Government of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh. Prior to aforesaid position the petitioners was posted in Bangladesh Embassy at Cairo, Egypt as 2nd Secretary and 1st Secretary in Abu Dhabi, UAE, as Consellor, in London, Embassy of Bangladesh, London. He was Minister and Charge d''Affaires of Bangladesh Embassy in Manila, the Philippines and lastly, he was serving as the Director General in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs at Dhaka as stated above. 

 3. The petitioner was also detained under the Special Powers Act and on a Writ Petition the Rule was made absolute and he was directed to be released by the High Court Division. But because of his arrest in the aforesaid criminal case he could not be released. It is further stated that since his arrest he is being kept in Dhaka Central Jail as an ordinary under-trial prisoner in a closed cell and in solitary confinement causing gradual decay to his health and drastic loss of weight. He has been kept in unhygienic and undesirable condition and in continuous solitary confinement since his arrest. He has been suffering from hypertension and high blood pressure and the treatment he needed is not available inside the jail. Due to prolonged detention the condition of his health has been deteriorating and he is being kept in custody in gross violation of the provisions of Jail Code and Human Rights. The petitioner applied on a number of times, to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, for giving him Division-I, but the same were refused. It is further stated that when he, applied to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, for Class-I status in the jail in the month of March 1997, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate called for a report from the Officer-in-Charge, Gulshan Police Station about the status and condition of the petitioner. But unfortunately, till today no report was sent by the officer-in-charge Gulshan Police Station as per direction of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. A number of times the petitioner prayed for Division-I in the jail showing his status and family condition, but on different grounds the same were refused by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate and these orders of refusal have been annexed with this petition as annexures. Ultimately, the petitioner filed an application before the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka, being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3416 of 1997. But by an order dated 21-8-97 the learned Sessions Judge Dhaka, refused to entertain the application on the ground that it was premature. Then the petitioner moved this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure whereupon the present Rule has been issued. 

 "910(1) Under-trial prisoners shall be divided into two Divisions, viz, Division I under-trial and Division II under-trial. Division I under-trial shall include all prisoners who by social status, education and habit of life have been accustomed to a superior mode of living, while Division II under-trial shall include prisoners whose status and mode of living are not superior to the ordinary and who are consequently not eligible for Division 1. The classification of under-trial will be done by the trying Courts subject to the approval of the District Magistrate, or in the case of Calcutta, the Chief Presidency Magistrate, and the previous standard of living will be the sole eriterion. 

 5. Mr Shahabuddin Ahmad, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the opposite-parties, opposes this Rule stating that this application is not maintainable inasmuch as in a case like this the High Court Division should not exercise its inherent power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further submits that it is upto the trying Court and the District Magistrate to decide as to whether the Division I should be given to an under-trial prisoner or not. He frankly submits that the petitioner is a man of status, no doubt, but this application is not maintainable and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 6. Paragraph 910 of the Jail Code provides that the trying Court shall consider the question of giving Division to an under-trial prisoner subject to approval of the District Magistrate. It is a peculiar case inasmuch as in the instant case the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate in seisin of the whole case and the charge-sheet has not yet been submitted in the instant case. On several'' occasions prayer was made to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka, for giving him Division-I in the Dhaka Central Jail, but on several grounds he rejected the application of the petitioner. Further, it appears that in the month of March, 1997, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka directed the Officer-in-Charge, Gulshan Police Station to give a report about the status of the petitioner. But unfortunately, no report was sent by the Officer-in-charge of the Gulshan Police Station to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. Finding no other way the petitioner moved learned Sessions Judge for appropriate relief. But the learned Sessions Judge passed the order on 21-5-97 stating that the application was pre-mature. Law provides that the trying Court will give permission for Division I in the jail to an under-trial prisoner with the approval of the District Magistrate. But, in the instant case, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate is, in fact, avoiding to pass an order on flimsy grounds and as such the question of approval by the District Magistrate does not arise in such peculiar circumstances. The petitioner had no other alternative but to invoke the inherent Jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code -of Criminal Procedure for ends of Justice. In view of the above, we find that the Objection raised by the learned Deputy Attorney-General has no substance and we hold that this application is maintainable. 

 7. Mr Mahabubur Rahman submits that he is the lawyer of the present petitioner who is an accused in jail killing case, namely, Lalbagh PS Case No. 11 (Il)75 relating to the indident of jail killing which took place on 3-11-1975. He further submits that Bangabandhu Murder Case is being tried by the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka, and he is also appearing as lawyer for some of the accused of that Bangabandhu Murder Case. He further submits that some of the accused of Bangabandhu Murder Case who are also co-accused with the petitioner in the jail killing case have already been granted Division-I in the Dhaka Central Jail and, as such, he is praying before this Court for Division-I for the present petitioner who is on the same footing with some of the accused who are being tried in Bangabandhu Murder Case. As regards the family status and standard of living of the present petitioner, the learned Deputy Attorney-General frankly submits that he is entitled to have Division I in jail as per Paragraph 910 of the Jail Code. It appears to us also that earlier he was an army officer. Then he served for several years in different embassies of Bangladesh abroad and then he was Minister and Charged Affairs of the Bangladesh Embassy in Manila, the Philippines and lastly, before his arrest, he was the Director General with the rank and status of the Joint Secretary of the Government serving in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. So, we hold that he is entitled to have the Division-for Class I status in the jail as under-trial prisoner under the provisions of Paragraph 910 of the Jail Code. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as stated above, we are of the view that this Rule should be made absolute. 

 In the result, this Rule is made absolute and the opposite-parties are directed to grant Division I status to the petitioner in the Dhaka Central Jail as under-trial prisoner in connection with Lalbagh PS Case No. 11(11)75 till the disposal of that case.
